description:
About Life360

Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 107.7 million monthly active users (MAU), as of September 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries.  

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com.

Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above. 

We are AI Native

We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

About The Team

The Connected Devices team at Life360 owns end-to-end device software readiness across our portfolio — firmware, app, and cloud engineering working as one team to ship the trackers and wearables that keep families connected to the people, pets, and things they care about most. We're not just a firmware team: we own the full device software stack, from the hardware modules to the cloud, across the whole lifecycle — architecture and hardware bring-up through mass production and post-launch refinement.

We're moving toward a more intelligent hardware ecosystem — processing continuous multi-sensor telemetry on the device itself, in real time, within tight power and memory budgets. We're an AI-Native engineering team: AI isn't just a tool we use, it's how we work — across specifications, code, test, review, data analysis and triage. Today that means firmware running across our Tile and Pet GPS tracker lines — devices shipping in the hundreds of thousands of units.

This role reports to the Engineering Manager, Connected Devices, and works day-to-day alongside our firmware, app, and cloud engineers, quality assurance, data science, hardware, operations, and data teams.

About the Job

We're looking for a Senior Firmware Engineer II to drive low-level embedded execution, security, and hardware integration across Life360's connected devices portfolio.

You are a firmware engineer with deep roots in Electrical Engineering. In this role, application code is secondary—your primary mandate is low-level firmware architecture, hardware EE collaboration, and wireless robustness. "Senior II" means you take high ownership of complex technical challenges across the stack. You can dive into schematic reviews, troubleshoot board-level anomalies, secure communications, manage low-level RF control, or optimize radio coexistence, flexing seamlessly across new product development and fleet maintenance as priorities shift.

For candidates based in the US, the salary range for this position is $109,500 to $199,500 USD. For candidates based out of Canada, the salary range for this position is 158,500 to 185,000 CAD. Note: Please be aware that the job title for positions in Canada will be "Developer" in lieu of "Engineer." We take into consideration an individual's background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers.

Total compensation is inclusive of equity compensation in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), as well as a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, financial, and other benefits.

What You’ll Do

Drive Low-Level Firmware & Hardware Integration

  • Develop and maintain low-level drivers, DMA pipelines, and peripheral interfaces (GPIO, I²C, SPI, UART) across RTOS and bare-metal environments (Zephyr, FreeRTOS, ThreadX).
  • Implement reliable on-device storage architectures, flash wear-leveling strategies, and efficient Inter-Process Communication (IPC).
  • Partner closely with EE on schematic reviews, hardware validation, and building hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) stress test rigs to verify edge-case stability.

Secure the Device Ecosystem

  • Architect and maintain device security pipelines, covering AWS IoT authentication, cryptographic key storage, encryption, and signed, rollback-protected OTA updates.

Optimize RF Performance & Compliance

  • Implement low-level RF control schemes and support GNSS assistance pipelines.
  • Mitigate wireless coexistence challenges across BLE and Wi-Fi to ensure stable concurrent connections.
  • Write RF compliance firmware to pass global regulatory standards and manage formal FCC/CE compliance testing requirements.

Work AI-Natively and Support the Fleet

  • Leverage AI development tools daily to accelerate prototyping, code review, documentation, and root-cause analysis.
  • Share technical ownership of shipped products by participating in on-call rotations, field triage, and team code reviews.

What We’re Looking For

Foundation & Core Technical Bar

  • 7+ years of embedded firmware experience shipping production consumer devices at scale.
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
  • Deep proficiency in C/C++ and practical, hands-on experience with RTOS internals (Zephyr, FreeRTOS, ThreadX) or bare-metal embedded architectures.
  • Strong EE fundamentals: ability to read schematics, evaluate power trees, and debug hardware hands-on using oscilloscopes and logic analyzers.
  • Direct experience with flash storage management and low-level peripheral buses (GPIO, I²C, SPI, UART).

Security Track Record

  • Demonstrated background deploying on-device security (secure boot, key provisioning, encryption) and integrating with cloud security backends (such as AWS IoT).

Wireless & RF Expertise

  • Prior experience shipping multi-radio wireless devices (BLE, Wi-Fi, GNSS).
  • Hands-on experience with low-level RF control and calibration.
  • Proven ability to navigate RF regulatory compliance labs, including managing FCC/CE compliance testing.

Nice to Have Qualifications

  • Experience integrating cloud/app endpoints and designing complex firmware state machines.
  • Deep power management profiling (sleep modes) and hardware/software watchdog implementations.
  • Exposure to Cellular (LTE-M/NB-IoT) integration or manufacturing test line bring-up.

AI-Native Expectations

  • Daily use — you use AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent) every day for real firmware work: drafting and refactoring code, debugging on-device failures, writing specs and design docs. This isn’t autocomplete; it’s a standing part of how you work.
  • Judgment and ownership — you review every line of AI-generated code as critically as you would a human PR before it ships to a device in the field. The AI writes it; you’re accountable for it.
  • Velocity — you’re expected to use AI to compress timelines that used to take weeks, from specifications to working prototype to validated on-device behavior, and to be able to explain your approach when you don’t.
  • Team leadership — you share what you learn (patterns that work, guardrails you’ve added, failure modes you’ve hit) through code review, design docs, and pairing, and you help raise the team’s AI fluency, not just your own.
  • Continuous learning — you stay current on embedded-AI tooling and techniques and bring recommendations back to the team rather than waiting for them to arrive.

Our Benefits

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans (100% paid for US employees). We offer life and disability as well as supplemental plans for medical and dental for Canadian employees.
  • 401(k) plan with company matching program in the US and RRSP with DPSP plan for Canadian employees.
  • Paid parental leave.
  • Mental Wellness Program & Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental well-being.
  • Generous time off: flexible PTO, companywide holidays throughout the year plus summer and winter shutdowns.
  • Learning & Development programs.
  • Equipment, tools, and reimbursement support for a productive remote environment.
  • Free Life360 Platinum Membership and Tile trackers.

AI Usage: We use AI to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Life360 hiring teams

Life360 Values

Our company’s mission-driven culture is guided by our shared values to create a trusted work environment where you can bring your authentic self to work and make a positive difference 

  • Be a Good Person - We have a team of high integrity people you can trust. 
  • Be Direct With Respect - We communicate directly, even when it’s hard.
  • Members Before Metrics - We focus on building an exceptional experience for families. 
  • High Intensity, High Impact - We do whatever it takes to get the job done. 

Our Commitment to Belonging

Life360 is an equal opportunity employer. We don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other legally protected status. We believe diverse perspectives make us better, and we’re building a workplace that reflects the communities we serve. Don’t meet every qualification? Apply anyway.
